Medical AI startup Boltz raises $110M to speed up small molecule research

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (840 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Boltz PBC, a startup that develops artificial intelligence models for pharmaceutical researchers, has raised $110 million in funding.
  • It has been revealed that bessemer led the Series A investment.
  • Small molecules, the building blocks of many drugs, can only neutralize a pathogen after binding to it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 16:17 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

Boltz PBC, a startup that develops artificial intelligence models for pharmaceutical researchers, has raised $110 million in funding.

It has been revealed that bessemer led the Series A investment. Boltz stated on Wednesday that the fund was joined by a large group of latest and returning backers. The consortium included Greycroft, Andreessen Horowitz, Amplify Partners, F-Prime Capital, Hummingbird and others.

Small molecules, the building blocks of many drugs, can only neutralize a pathogen after binding to it. As a result, researchers start drug discovery projects by looking for molecules that have a high binding affinity with pathogens. They often review hundreds of thousands of candidate molecules per project. The process can take months and often costs millions of dollars.

Boltz offers an AI model called BoltzMol-1 that speeds up the workflow. It generates binding affinity data by reviewing only a few dozen, particularly promising molecules instead of the hundreds of thousands usually needed. The fewer molecules need to be studied, the less time the analysis takes.

Binding affinity evaluations don’t yield drug discoveries right away. Instead, they produce data points called small molecule hits. Those are essentially faint clues that help researchers pinpoint the area where they should focus their efforts.

Boltz staffers asked BoltzMol-1 to look for small molecule hits across 10 “challenging and therapeutically-relevant targets.” Targets are biological building blocks that play a role in disease processes. According to the tech giant, the model found small molecule hits for six of the targets.

Scientists can adapt BoltzMol-1 to project-specific constraints. If a research team has access to a relatively limited number of compounds, it could configure the model to only consider small molecules that can be made from those compounds. When material procurement is not an obstacle, BoltzMol-1 evaluates a much larger number of candidates.

Sources indicate that the tech giant also offers a second model called BoltzProt-1. It can generate tens of thousands of protein designs based on data gleaned from small molecule hits. Additionally, BoltzProt-1 automatically reviews each protein to determine if it could be used to develop a new drug.

Sources indicate that usually, AI models evaluate protein designs based on rubrics that provide only an indirect view of their effectiveness. BoltzProt-1 uses more direct metrics. The firm indicates that BoltzProt-1’s protein evaluation mechanism demonstrated “higher success” than several competing models during internal tests.

Boltz sells its algorithms via an application programming interface that is billed based on token usage. According to the firm, customers’ token consumption has grown by a factor of 50 since BoltzMol-1 and BoltzProt-1 launched in June. Boltz counts six of the world’s 20 largest pharmaceutical companies as clients.

It has been revealed that the company will use its newly introduced funding to grow its headcount and procure more computing infrastructure. The extra hardware should make it easier for Boltz to keep up with leading AI labs such as newly public Anthropic PBC and OpenAI Group. Over the past year, both companies have introduced models that are highly adapted to biology research tasks.

Boltz has already started training a newly introduced generation of molecule design algorithms. The organization indicates that they are “showing substantial improvements” over its current models.

Restoring trust: Embattled CDC, HHS officials on their priorities for 2027

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that centers for Disease Control and Prevention Director Erica Schwartz, M.D., and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F.
  • In a fireside chat, a chipper Schwartz tried to answer a tough line of questioning about Americans’ loss of trust in her agency, controversial vaccine changes, measles and other public health complications.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes
Restoring trust: Embattled CDC, HHS officials on their priorities for 2027" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Federal health officials are focused on rebuilding trust with the public and working across the aisle with the latest Congress.

Recent findings suggest that centers for Disease Control and Prevention Director Erica Schwartz, M.D., and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., spoke at the Milken Institute’s Future of Health Summit last week in Washington, D.C. Over 1,200 attendees gathered at the event, the theme of which was “better health within reach.”.

In a fireside chat, a chipper Schwartz tried to answer a tough line of questioning about Americans’ loss of trust in her agency, controversial vaccine changes, measles and other public health complications.

According to recent reports, when asked about her potential disagreements with Kennedy, Schwartz stated, “I disagree all the time. He’s a lawyer, I’m a lawyer. […] What I love about the secretary is that he listens to those disagreements. He's not someone who just indicates, ‘No, I don't have room for that.’ He really does value differing opinions.”.

Industry observers note that the U.S. has lost its measles elimination status, global health officials revealed just this week. On that glitch, Schwartz stressed the importance of supporting CDC’s state partners on awareness, prevention and surveillance efforts.

“MMR is the number one way to prevent measles,” Schwartz mentioned. Today’s outbreaks “happen in communities that are very close-knit communities … that typically do not and have not vaccinated their children,” she said. Most cases are at the moment among kids over the age of five and adults, according to Schwartz.

Industry observers note that under Schwartz’s leadership, the CDC changed its method of reporting measles deaths from real-time reporting by state public health departments to death certificate data, which can face multi-month lags. Schwartz is being investigated by Energy & Commerce Committee Democrats who, during a briefing on CDC’s alleged suppression of the total number of national measles deaths on its dashboard, have called her unresponsive and misleading.

“As the crisis worsens, we are concerned that you continue to direct an effort at CDC to downplay the outbreak and artificially reduce the number of measles deaths that CDC reports to the public, concealing the fact that 10 people have died of measles-related deaths this year alone,” the Committee leaders wrote (PDF) in a letter on Tuesday. “We are expanding our investigation to examine the threat your actions pose to Americans’ health and whether changes to your statutory authority are required.”.

According to recent reports, during her fireside chat, Schwartz acknowledged that "we've lost trust not only externally with the American public, but also internally with the team that works at the CDC,” she noted. To address this, Schwartz wants the public to understand that CDC follows the science, is being transparent and “leading with humility.” She pointed to COVID-era “arrogance” from institutions, directing at instead of conversing with the public.

“I want to be a CDC director that really has a conversation with the American public,” Schwartz said.

According to recent reports, internally, the first priority is to add stability to the body, including hiring leaders within the agency so they have a permanent leadership role. The CDC has also created a strategic hiring plan for 2027 with the input of staff and is looking to its “force extenders” like epidemic intelligence officers and its Public Health Associate Program.

On how she’s planning to work with the new majority-Democratic Congress, Schwartz noted she was encouraged to see more Congress members coming in with a healthcare background, “who understand how these policies will impact patients.” She noted is eager to work with the Congressional Doctors Caucus and to work with both sides of the aisle.

“I know that we may not agree on every issue, but I do think there's a common ground where we can actually focus on really trying to make Americans healthy again,” she mentioned.

One of her priorities for 2027 is having a “21st-century CDC” by bringing innovation into the public health sphere. She called out the Biothreat Radar, a proposed wastewater surveillance program about which she recently spoke with Sen. Andy Kim (D-New Jersey). The program’s proposed (PDF) budget is $52 million. The CDC has also tentatively put out a call for new Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) members, which will depend on a final ruling from the appellate court in the agency’s favor.

Sources indicate that at the Summit, Schwartz’s comments did not necessarily satisfy some of the attendees. When asked by Fierce Healthcare for his impressions of the interview, a public health worker in the room who did not wish to be named called her a “traitor.".

In his fireside chat closing out the Summit, Secretary Kennedy primarily spoke about food and obesity.

One of HHS' most consequential accomplishments during his tenure, Kennedy stated, has been changing the dietary guidelines to be “science-based.” Earlier this year, the White House released new federal dietary guidelines, calling for prioritizing quality protein, healthy fats, fruits, vegetables and whole grains, while avoiding highly processed foods and refined carbs.

The agency is focused on transforming food across a number of sectors, including in Head Start programs—free federal early childhood programs—which have received about $151 million in supplemental HHS awards to strengthen nutrition services. HHS is also focused on rolling out healthy food options in the military, Kennedy stated, and within SNAP by allowing states to request waivers to restrict what SNAP dollars are spent on. As of this summer, HHS has released a Make Hospital Food Healthier Pledge, challenging hospitals to put nutrition at the center of patient care. HHS has also encouraged medical schools to increase their number of education hours on nutrition from an average of two to 40 hours, Kennedy said.

“Real” food sales in grocery stores, Kennedy claimed, went up 8% this year, while obesity rates have dropped by 7%. He acknowledged that the drop in obesity rates is more likely due to GLP-1 access rather than healthier eating. “If we can reduce obesity, we can reduce our healthcare costs,” he stated, praising Trump’s Most Favored Nation negotiations for lowering the price of drugs like Ozempic.

“We reward people at every level—the hospitals, the providers, other providers, doctors, insurance companies, pharmaceutical companies—we reward them financially for keeping people sick. And as long as those financial incentives are in place, we are going to be operating a sick-care system rather than a healthcare system,” Kennedy mentioned. HHS has started to change that by shifting more to value-based care, he added, so stakeholders get paid to keep patients healthy “rather than being paid to keep them sick.”.

Recent findings suggest that when asked what he wants his legacy as Health Secretary to be, Kennedy echoed Schwartz on the idea of following science. “What I want to do is to end corporate capture and the politicization of science … that Americans once again trust the regulatory agencies, they trust the science that’s coming from them,” he said.

Recent findings suggest that he referred to newer guidelines meant to encourage extra transparency from researchers. In 2026, the HHS Scientific Integrity Policy was updated (PDF) to support publishing raw data and code in publicly accessible repositories, preregistering study protocols and transparently reporting all results.

He noted he wants "to make sure that we’re not kowtowing to the food industry, the pharmaceutical industry, all these people who are at the trough taking on the $2.3 trillion that my agency gives out every year. And that instead, that Americans believe that this agency is devoted to their health, that they trust it, and that we are doing the science that we need to find out what is making them sick so that we can all eliminate it as a society.”.

Kennedy's interview at the event did not touch on measles or vaccine policy, where the secretary's policies and communications have garnered broader criticism and controversy than his views on nutrition. Tuesday's announcement that the U.S. had lost its measles elimination status garnered a fresh call for Kennedy's resignation among his critics, including the Democratic Doctors Caucus.

Also coinciding with Milken's event was the announcement of the inaugural 2027 cohort of the Elevate Investment Initiative. The effort, part of the Milken Institute’s Women Health Network, aims to mobilize $1 billion in net-new capital for women’s health innovation. The 10 fund managers and companies include Borski Fund, Cross-Border Impact Ventures, Foreground Capital, Meridian Health Ventures, How Women Invest and more. [cut this or move?].

7 Long Distance-Focused EV SUVs Ranked From Best To Worst Range

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2431 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, both average newly introduced-car prices and fuel prices are hitting record highs left and right.
  • It has been revealed that however, despite some highly competitive offerings, EVs haven't quite popped off yet.
  • Recent findings suggest that concerns about the range of EVs may have once been well-founded, but that's not so much the case anymore.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, both average newly introduced-car prices and fuel prices are hitting record highs left and right. The state of things would be enough to get any car enthusiast down, if it weren't for the fact that electric cars are rad as hell. Fast, stylish, and fuel-efficient, EVs seem to get better with each new model that is released and each new generation that refines an already good vehicle into something great (we're looking at you, Toyota bZ).

It has been revealed that however, despite some highly competitive offerings, EVs haven't quite popped off yet. The Trump administration's brutal murder of the EV tax credit and subsequent loosening of CAFE standards didn't help. The technology is still relatively newly introduced, so EVs are generally more expensive upfront than gas-powered cars, and there's also the question of range, one of the major specters haunting EV adoption at larger scales.

Recent findings suggest that concerns about the range of EVs may have once been well-founded, but that's not so much the case anymore. Tons of electric vehicles, SUVs included, can now breach 300 miles on a charge, and several are pushing past the 400-mile boundary, too. With ranges like that, road tripping is more than feasible, say nothing of the 34 miles the average American drives per day.

In a recent development, to illustrate the point, we've gathered a list of seven electric SUVs with excellent ranges — all over 300 miles on a full charge. This isn't a comprehensive list, but rather a sampling of the field, from awe-inspiring Lucids to affordable-ish Fords. To make the list, the cars needed an official fuel economy estimate published by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). Perhaps unsurprisingly, more range is typically more expensive, and the longest-range SUVs out there are luxury vehicles, but a few more accessible rides made the list, too.

Debuting for the 2027 model year, the BMW iX5 is a shakeup to the luxury EV SUV world in a couple of big ways. For starters, this is the German automaker's first electric iteration of the popular (but once-controversial) X5. Iterating on a beloved idea is always sure to ruffle some feathers, but actually driving the iX5 might just unruffle those feathers right back down. The iX5 is also one of the exceedingly few EV SUVs that come close to matching the range of the Lucid Gravity. However, the iX5 actually dethrones the Gravity and takes the top spot among long-distance-focused EV SUVs. The icing on the iX5 cake is that it somehow manages to be even cheaper than its Lucid rival.

Industry observers note that there's only one version of the BMW iX5 for its inaugural year, known as the iX5 60 xDrive, and it MSRPs at $81,250 with the destination fee included. This leaves the iX5 around $20,000 cheaper than the Lucid Gravity with the longest range. That's an impressive accomplishment, even if the iX5 doesn't quite stack up in other ways. To get the full 456 miles of range, you'll need to opt for BMW's 21-inch M Aero Polygon 1116 M wheels or the 21-inch Aero Double-Spoke Bicolor 1113 wheels with summer tires that can be chosen for no additional cost. Other available wheels result in a range from 418 miles to 447 miles. Still not bad.

When it comes to performance and style, the iX5 feels distinctly X5-like, though it reportedly doesn't handle quite as well. BMW advertises a 0-60 mph time of 4.4 seconds, which is slower than some rivals, and the iX5 also has less cargo space than the Gravity. Features abound, and the interior is comfortable and stylish.

Lucid Motors flipped the American EV world on its head when it debuted the Lucid Air, which had a maximum range of up to 517 miles. Then the mad lads did it again with the Lucid Gravity, which held the record for the longest-range SUV until the BMW iX5 came onto the scene. Still, the Gravity is a lot more than just an exceptionally long-range SUV that, admittedly, looks like a cooler minivan.

Sources indicate that in our test, we found that the Gravity is just hands-down exceptional. The SUV has also earned astounding 10/10 ratings from both Car and Driver and U.S. News & World Report, and it consistently lands among the top two or three entries in its class in other major publications. It's lauded for its alacrity off the line, generous cargo area, and its refined interior.

To get the most range possible, you'll need to get your hands on the mid-tier Grand Touring trim and keep the standard wheels, which are 20 inches in the front and 21 inches in the back. Other wheel options are available but reduce your overall range. This setup will run you $98,900 plus the $1,600 destination fee, which puts the Lucid Gravity GT just within the six-figure range before tax. In return, you get a screaming-fast 3.4-second 0-60 mph time, 828 horsepower, and the ability to charge up to 200 miles in under 11 minutes. And you get to drive one of the coolest cars on the road today.

Standard features on the Gravity GT include PerLuxe leather upholstery, 12-way power-adjustable front seats, a power liftgate, a 34-inch cockpit display, a 12.6-inch landscape pilot display, a wireless charging pad, a 10-speaker stereo, and tons of safety and driver assistance features. All-wheel drive is standard, but the optional third row reduces the range to 437 miles.

Sources indicate that the final 400-mile top dog on this list is the illustrious Rivian R1S. While Rivian has just recently dropped the smaller and better-than-we-ever-hoped-for 2027 R2 and has some of us biting our nails in anticipation of the smaller-yet R3, enthusiasts would be remiss to forget that the R1S is still a wildly impressive machine with monstrous off-road capabilities and up to a delicious 410 miles of maximum range. And on top of that, the R1S was one of just two large SUVs to earn the IIHS Top Safety Pick+ designation in 2026.

In a recent development, another aspect that sets the R1S apart from its long-range competition is its status as a default seven-seater. While the Lucid Gravity offers an optional third row, the R1S is designed for it natively, and it's all the better for it. All three rows have adult-friendly legroom, even if getting all the way back takes some squeezing. The 2027 R1S starts at $85,885 for the base Premium trim with destination, and unlocking the full range requires upgrading to the long-range battery, which costs an extra $7,000. The setup produces 533 horsepower and can hustle from 0-60 mph in 4.5 seconds.

The interior is spacious and comfortable, offering abundant head- and legroom in the first two rows and well-cushioned seats. The design aesthetic is modern and distinctly premium, featuring metal and wood accents and soft plastics. It's the electro-minimalism we're used to by now but done superbly. The R1S can tow up to 7,700 pounds when properly equipped and also has off-road chops for days, thanks to its high torque rating, good ground clearance and standard surround-view camera system. Like many EVs, it's screen-forward, almost obnoxiously so, but that's a small price to pay for greatness.

In a recent development, say what you will about Tesla — from dodging hundreds of millions of dollars in taxes probably being a bad thing to the organization's vehicles' being inextricably linked to Elon Musk's questionable politics — but the fallen automaker did help pave the way for some of the truly exceptional EVs we have today, and the Tesla Model Y was no small part of that. You can yet see some of that luster in the Model Y's still-impressive range of up to 355 miles — 3 miles more than the larger Model X's 352-mile maximum.

According to recent reports, the Model Y's range is a steep drop from the other luxury EV SUVs on this list, but it's important to remember that the above entries are the crème de la crème – the boundary-pushing pinnacle of EV design and the culmination of years and billions of dollars of R&D. They are, simply put, outliers among electric SUVs. Meanwhile, 355 miles of range is still far more than the majority of the field. And while the Model Y loses 55 miles of range compared to the R1S and its ilk, this Tesla is drastically less expensive up front. For the full 355-mile range, you'll need the standard-wheelbase Model Y Premium with rear-wheel drive, which runs a mere $47,630 with destination.

Recent findings suggest that the downside, of course, is that you own a Tesla in a reality where the CEO appeared to have publicly thrown up a Sieg Heil. While the Model Y was once the world's best-selling car, it's been surpassed by many rivals in recent years. It has been knocked for its cumbersome touch controls, a stiff ride, and lots of cheap-feeling plastics. Sure, even the Long-Range Model Y Premium can sprint from 0-60 mph in 5.4 seconds (4.3 seconds with AWD), and has a spacious interior, but that's not particularly special anymore.

Hyundai has been killing it in the electrification game recently, and the Ioniq 9's introduction for the 2026 model year took the company's cred even higher. Made stateside, the Ioniq 9 is the most expensive Hyundai ever, with a starting price of $60,655 after destination fees. And while that's pretty pricey, you sure do get what you pay for. There's tons of space for both passengers and cargo, and the interior design is sleek and modern. It's also a three-row ride with room for six or seven, depending on the configuration, and the third row is largely adult-friendly. I'm a serial third-row hater, and I adored my time spent in the way back on the Ioniq 9. It's even easy to access, which earns it major points in my book.

Recent findings suggest that the lineup's best range of 335 miles is found on the base S trim, which uses a single-motor rear-wheel-drive setup that produces 215 hp and 258 lb-ft of torque. That's a lot less power than what you'll find above, meaning the Ioniq 9 is one of the slowest SUVs on this list, but a decent torque rating means it won't feel sluggish from a stop. Somewhat surprisingly, upgrading to a dual-motor trim with all-wheel drive only reduces the range by 15 miles while bumping the power output up to 303 hp, and it costs just $3,810 extra, which might just be worth it depending on how badly you need the extra range.

Sources indicate that standard features on the base S trim include cloth upholstery, heated seats, an eight-way power-adjustable driver's seat, a 12.3-inch touch screen, a wireless charging pad, and a whole seven USB-C ports. Factor in the Ioniq 9's long list of ADAS features, like Hyundai's Highway Driving Assist 2, pedestrian and cyclist detection, and traffic-sign recognition, and the price starts to feel justified.

While you might balk at seeing the beloved Mustang name slapped on an electric SUV of all things (an SUV Mustang? Make it make sense!), this Ford actually is the real deal. When we talk about well-rounded cars, this is what we mean. Heck, the 2027 Ford Mustang Mach-E even has a soft-roader trim. The Mustang Mach-E is screaming fast, super charismatic, fun to drive, spacious, relatively affordable, and long-ranged. Finding something to dislike about this SUV involves a level of nitpicking that isn't worth getting into here. If you haven't found yourself inside a Mustang Mach-E, reserve all judgment until you do, and get in one as soon as possible.

Industry observers note that to get the most out of the Mustang Mach-E's range, you'll need to get the rear-wheel-drive Premium model with the extended battery pack, which unlocks the full 320-mile range. The Premium trim starts at $41,090 and carries a $2,045 destination fee, while the battery upgrade costs an extra $4,750. This version of the Mustang Mach-E sports 272 hp and 387 lb-ft of torque, which is more than enough to make this crossover feel truly fun.

Sources indicate that the interior is upholstered with synthetic leather, and it's known to be comfortable and spacious in both rows, though you may want to stick to a maximum capacity of four due to the center column eating some of the rear middle legroom. The cabin design is centered around the Ford's 15.5-inch touch screen, which is vertically mounted and controls many car functions in addition to infotainment. Other standard features on the Premium trim include dual-zone automatic climate control, power-adjustable front seats with heating and ventilation, and ambient interior lighting. Despite the Mustang Mach-E not having seen a refresh in a few years, it still feels stylish and modern.

It has been revealed that coming in just shy of the Mustang Mach-E's 320-mile range is the 2027 Chevrolet Equinox EV at a very respectable 319 miles. The Chevy Equinox EV is what you might call the people's car. It's the least expensive SUV on this list by a few thousand bucks and a somewhat modest offering compared to the rest of the entries here, but it's by no measure a poor choice for EV shoppers.

In a recent development, the base LT 1 trim starts at $37,195 with destination. It's one of very few EVs under $40,000 that gets over 300 miles on a single charge, and you can get that mileage on any trim with front-wheel drive. Models with all-wheel drive lose about 12 miles of range, leaving them still solidly above the crucial 300-mile mark.

The best way to describe the Equinox EV is perhaps to call it familiar and predictable. There's not much flashy about it, and it's not particularly sprightly with its 220 horsepower. Testers report the Equinox EV rides smoothly with engaging handling, but notably heavy understeer takes some joy out of taking the SUV through corners. However, as a practical car used for commuting, city driving, and the occasional road trip, there's not much to actively dislike. The interior is spacious, albeit not exactly beautiful, and even tall passengers will have space in the back row. The Equinox EV also dodged Chevy's recent EV recall involving faulty brakes, which is a big point in its favor.

According to recent reports, on the base LT 1 trim, you'll get features like cloth upholstery, manually adjustable front seats, a couple USB ports, and a 17.7-inch touch screen. Safety features include forward collision alert, rear park assist, and Teen Driver mode.

Breaking: Even occasional marijuana use linked to 40% higher odds of stroke

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1414 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • New preliminary research involving more than 440,000 American adults has uncovered a concerning association between cannabis use and cardiovascular disease, particularly stroke.
  • The research, presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026, found that the association was not limited to people who frequently used cannabis.
  • Scientific Sessions 2026 took place November 6 through 9 in Chicago, bringing together cardiovascular researchers and healthcare professionals from around the world to share scientific discoveries, clinical advances, and emerging evidence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

New preliminary research involving more than 440,000 American adults has uncovered a concerning association between cannabis use and cardiovascular disease, particularly stroke. The findings suggest that even occasional marijuana use may be linked to higher odds of cardiovascular problems, raising new questions about the health effects of a substance that is becoming increasingly common across the United States.

The research, presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026, found that the association was not limited to people who frequently used cannabis. It also appeared across different methods of consumption (smoked or edible, etc.). Researchers emphasized that cannabis use should be considered when discussing heart health and stroke prevention.

Scientific Sessions 2026 took place November 6 through 9 in Chicago, bringing together cardiovascular researchers and healthcare professionals from around the world to share scientific discoveries, clinical advances, and emerging evidence.

Cannabis refers to the plant itself, while marijuana is a commonly used term for cannabis products containing enough THC to produce psychoactive effects.

Marijuana Use Is Rising Across the United States.

"Previous research has indicated that cannabis use is rapidly increasing in the United States, with 1 in 6 adults in 2024 reporting having used it within the last month, up from 1 in 10 in 2020 -- a 51% increase," stated study author Aabha Divya, M.B.B.S., M.Ch., an assistant professor in the division of cardiothoracic surgery at the Tulane University School of Medicine in Newly introduced Orleans.

Sources indicate that earlier research conducted between 2016 and 2020 had already identified associations between cannabis consumption and unfavorable cardiovascular outcomes. Those findings also suggested that using cannabis more frequently during a given month was connected to greater cardiovascular risk.

In a recent development, however, the evidence has not always been consistent. With recreational marijuana becoming legal in more places and cannabis products increasingly available, Divya and colleagues wanted to investigate these possible health effects in a larger population.

Sources indicate that "We wanted to expand on this earlier work because cannabis use has become increasingly common in the United States, as recreational legalization and commercial availability of various products with cannabis have also expanded. Previous studies have raised concerns about possible cardiovascular effects; however, the results have not been consistent," Divya remarked.

Sources indicate that the researchers examined information collected through the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS), a large telephone survey of American adults. They combined responses from jurisdictions that collected information about cannabis consumption between 2020 and 2024.

Participants answered questions about their marijuana use and whether a healthcare professional had ever diagnosed them with cardiovascular conditions, including a heart attack, stroke, or coronary heart disease.

Even Occasional Marijuana Use Was Linked to Higher Stroke Odds.

In a recent development, one of the most striking findings was that infrequent cannabis use was associated with cardiovascular problems. In fact, the researchers did not find the steady increase in cardiovascular risk with more frequent use that they had expected.

The analysis revealed several key associations:.

These findings were unexpected because the relationship between cannabis use and cardiovascular disease did not consistently become stronger as consumption increased.

In a recent development, "We were surprised to find that the link between cannabis use and cardiovascular disease was not straightforward. We expected that the chances of heart disease would gradually rise as people used cannabis more often, but that wasn't the case. Both low-use and heavy-use groups had higher odds of developing heart disease," Divya stated.

Although the study cannot establish that marijuana directly causes strokes or other cardiovascular conditions, the findings suggest that occasional consumption should not automatically be considered free of potential cardiovascular concerns.

"As cannabis use becomes more common, it is increasingly vital that people and their healthcare professionals include it in conversations about cardiovascular health, just as they discuss tobacco, alcohol and other commonly used substances," she added.

Experts Urge Greater Attention to Cannabis and Heart Health.

It has been revealed that robert L. Page II, Pharm.D., M.S.P.H., FAHA, who led the writing group responsible for the American Heart Association's 2020 cannabis scientific statement, mentioned the findings add to growing concerns about marijuana's possible cardiovascular effects.

One challenge in evaluating those effects is that many cannabis owners also smoke tobacco. Because tobacco is already an established cardiovascular risk factor, separating its effects from those of cannabis can be difficult.

Page, who was not involved in the research, explained why the upcoming findings deserve attention.

"Unfortunately, many patients who use cannabis may also smoke tobacco, which completely clouds the problem when addressing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk. In patients who use both, cannabis has always been considered an innocent bystander; however, this is not the case. This is the second observational study to suggest that cannabis exposure (without tobacco smoking) may be a potential risk factor for developing cardiovascular disease. Overall, cannabis is beginning to emerge as a major contributor to premature heart disease in young and older adults, which can lead to serious cardiovascular events. To this end, clinicians should be addressing cannabis use with their patients as they would tobacco use when considering the risk of cardiovascular disease.".

Page is a professor in the department of clinical pharmacy and the department of physical medicine/rehabilitation at the University of Colorado Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences in Aurora, Colorado.

How Researchers Studied Nearly Half a Million Americans.

It has been revealed that the analysis included 442,906 adults living in the United States (average age of 49 years; approximately half women). Their responses came from telephone surveys conducted through the BRFSS.

In a recent development, researchers used survey information collected from 2020 through 2024, focusing on states that had included an optional marijuana questionnaire. Between 16 and 24 states participated in this portion of the survey each year, meaning the analysis did not represent every state.

It has been revealed that participants reported how many days they had consumed cannabis during the preceding month. The questions covered multiple ways of using marijuana (smoking, vaping or ingesting gummies or other cannabis-containing foods).

The researchers divided participants into four categories based on their reported use:.

Participants also indicated whether they had ever received a diagnosis of heart attack, heart disease, heart-related chest pain, or stroke.

Industry observers note that to better distinguish the association with cannabis from other potential explanations, the researchers accounted for numerous established cardiovascular risk factors. These included demographic characteristics, tobacco smoking, alcohol consumption, obesity, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, physical inactivity, education, and income.

Why the Findings Do Not Prove Marijuana Causes Strokes.

Despite the large number of participants, the study has several limitations that affect how its findings should be interpreted.

Sources indicate that first, the analysis examined associations between reported cannabis use and previously diagnosed cardiovascular conditions at a single point in time. This means researchers could not determine whether marijuana use preceded the cardiovascular problems or whether it directly contributed to them.

It has been revealed that the information also depended on participants accurately recalling and reporting their cannabis consumption and medical histories (making them subject to potential errors in memory). Such reports may not always reflect actual patterns of use or diagnoses.

Another limitation was the lack of information about the strength of the cannabis products participants consumed or the quantities they used. Without those details, the researchers could not evaluate whether THC potency or the amount consumed influenced the observed associations.

Industry observers note that the researchers also acknowledged that some participants may have reduced or discontinued cannabis consumption after being diagnosed with cardiovascular disease. As a result, the group reporting no cannabis use in the previous month may have included former owners.

Recent findings suggest that these uncertainties make it difficult to draw firm conclusions about how consumption frequency affects cardiovascular health. Nevertheless, the findings add to growing evidence that cannabis use deserves closer examination as a possible factor in heart disease and stroke.

As marijuana becomes more widely available and its use continues to increase, researchers and healthcare professionals are emphasizing the importance of discussing cannabis alongside other substances that may affect cardiovascular health.

The American Hospital Association (AHA) and West Health Institute confirmed Tuesday a new collaboration with medtech firm Becton, Dickinson and Company (BD) aimed at accelerating the adoption of technologies shown to improve patient care.

The collaboration builds on the West Health Accelerator at AHA’s Health Research & Educational Trust (HRET), a three-year initiative to aid healthcare organizations in scaling technology-enabled solutions.

It has been revealed that “No single organization can close the gap between innovation and everyday care on its own,” mentioned Zia Agha, M.D., West Health Institute chief medical officer, in a statement. “This collaboration brings hospital reach, clinical technology expertise and performance intelligence together from the start. We’re beginning with a focused group of hospitals, learning what it takes to make changes last, and building a model that can reach hospitals of every size and resource level.”.

In a recent development, the new collaboration will begin with an initial cohort of 10 hospitals and health systems. It will incorporate advanced physiologic monitoring with clinical protocols in practice, specifically targeting concerns associated with postoperative complications and longer hospital stays. Additionally, Vizient will provide performance benchmarking and analytic capabilities, the organizations stated.

Takeaways from the early cohort will help to identify adoption barriers, refine implementation approaches and outline necessary support to expand the model to a broader group.

BD Advanced Patient Monitoring Worldwide President Tim Patz noted in a statement that the company believes innovation “has the greatest impact when it translates into meaningful improvements in patient care.”.

Recent findings suggest that “Our experience working with healthcare systems has shown us the value of bringing together advanced hemodynamic monitoring, data and the expertise of hospital care teams to support better-informed patient care,” Patz said. “This collaboration gives us an opportunity to build on that experience, further integrate proven solutions into clinical practice and help more patients benefit from them.”.

It has been revealed that bitcoin price is getting hammered in the aftermath of the FOMC minutes. Gold isn’t doing much better; oil and stocks have joined the sell-off. The markets are already nervous about the Federal Reserve’s next decision, and yesterday’s FOMC minutes gave us another reason to worry: policymakers are still talking about raising interest rates.

In a recent development, almost all officials saw further hikes as appropriate under their baseline outlook. Two even floated the possibility of a bigger increase if inflation refuses to cool.

This is a nasty combination for markets. Bitcoin fell around 3.2% over 24 hours, gold futures dropped more than 3%, and WTI crude lost around 3%. The dollar climbed to a 19-month high. Wall Street was mixed, though, with the Nasdaq finishing higher while the Dow and S&P 500 slipped.

Sources indicate that here’s the comparison. In March 2020, the Fed was slashing rates, buying bonds and throwing emergency liquidity at a financial system under immense pressure. Congress approved a $2.2 trillion rescue package to keep households and businesses afloat.

Today, we are watching markets fall while the Fed is possibly making money more expensive.

In a recent development, october’s FOMC minutes weren’t exactly what markets wanted to hear. The Fed held rates at 3.75%–4% during its October meeting, but almost all participants believed further increases would likely be appropriate. Two officials also remarked a hike larger than the usual 25 basis points could be considered if inflation data came in hotter than expected.

And there was more in those minutes than just interest rates. Officials raised concerns about hedge fund leverage and the growing debt tied to artificial intelligence investments. Some financing arrangements could become a problem if investors start questioning enormous AI spending, and whether it will generate the returns companies expect.

The risk is forced selling. Leveraged funds facing losses or investor withdrawals may have to dump assets quickly, potentially pushing prices down further.

Recent findings suggest that gold has its own problem. A stronger dollar and higher interest rates make it less attractive to investors who can earn a return elsewhere. Bitcoin price, meanwhile, remains vulnerable when traders cut exposure to speculative assets.

The Fed hasn’t declared a financial emergency. Its minutes actually describe the banking system as resilient. But officials are clearly paying attention to risks that could amplify a market shock.

Discover: The Best Token Presales.

March 2020 was brutal. COVID-19 lockdowns brought businesses to a standstill. Investors rushed for cash, stocks collapsed, and Bitcoin briefly slipped below $4,000 after sitting near $10,000 just weeks earlier.

Recent findings suggest that the Federal Reserve didn’t wait around. It cut rates by 50 basis points on March 3, then delivered another 100-basis-point cut on March 15. The federal funds target range dropped to 0%–0.25%.

In a recent development, on March 23, the Fed unveiled unlimited purchases of Treasury securities and mortgage-backed securities, promising to buy whatever amounts were necessary to support market functioning. It also introduced emergency lending programmes to keep credit flowing.

Industry observers note that president Donald Trump signed the $2.2 trillion CARES Act on March 27. The package included direct payments to eligible Americans, expanded unemployment benefits, and assistance for businesses struggling to survive lockdowns. The Paycheck Protection Program gave small businesses access to loans designed to help them keep employees on payroll.

In a recent development, the response was enormous, but the economy was facing an extraordinary shutdown. Millions of Americans had lost their jobs, businesses were closing, and normal economic activity had practically disappeared.

Markets eventually bounced back. The S&P 500 recovered its pre-pandemic record by August 2020. Bitcoin climbed above $12,000 during the same month.

The current US economy isn’t in the same position as it was during the pandemic. Inflation remains above the Fed’s 2% target, and policymakers are discussing rate increases rather than cuts.

Industry observers note that slashing rates to zero and flooding markets with liquidity might help asset prices. It could also make inflation worse. Another multitrillion-dollar spending package would face an entirely different argument in Congress, especially without a pandemic-style economic shutdown.

Industry observers note that the Fed doesn’t have to choose between doing nothing and repeating the 2020 rescue. If banks struggle to fund themselves or credit markets start freezing, it can step in with emergency lending and liquidity operations. That’s a much narrower response than another round of unlimited bond purchases.

The Fed’s concerns about leveraged hedge funds and AI financing could become more relevant if investors start selling indiscriminately. A market correction is one thing. Forced selling spreading through the financial system is another.

At the moment, there’s no evidence that we’re facing another March 2020. The banking system remains resilient, and falling Bitcoin prices alone won’t trigger a government bailout.

But the Fed has a problem that didn’t exist in quite the same way during the pandemic. It may need to protect financial stability without giving up its fight against inflation. In 2020, Washington opened the taps. This time, we wait and see, and Bitcoin price will survive.

#110797. Energy drinks linked to 11 times more reports of cardiac arrest

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1372 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Energy drinks linked to 11 times more reports of cardiac arrest

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1372 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that energy drinks and stimulant supplements are raising fresh concerns about heart health after researchers discovered a striking pattern in reports of serious cardiovascular emergencies.
  • Industry observers note that the findings were particularly concerning among younger adults.
  • In a recent development, researchers emphasized that the findings do not establish that energy drinks or stimulant supplements caused these medical emergencies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that energy drinks and stimulant supplements are raising fresh concerns about heart health after researchers discovered a striking pattern in reports of serious cardiovascular emergencies. Products containing caffeine and other stimulants appeared far more frequently in reports of cardiac arrest, heart attacks, and other heart problems than products without these ingredients.

Industry observers note that the findings were particularly concerning among younger adults. People ages 18 to 34 accounted for a substantial share of the reported heart problems involving caffeinated products, according to independent, preliminary research presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026.

In a recent development, researchers emphasized that the findings do not establish that energy drinks or stimulant supplements caused these medical emergencies. However, the unusually high frequency of certain cardiovascular events in FDA safety reports suggests that these widely available products deserve closer examination.

Growing Concerns About Energy Drinks and Heart Health.

According to recent reports, the energy drink industry has expanded rapidly, with sales more than doubling over the past decade and exceeding $20 billion in 2024. Despite their popularity, scientists still have limited information about the cardiovascular effects of energy drinks and supplements containing stimulants.

Existing evidence suggests that consuming large amounts of caffeine can harm the cardiovascular system. Medical professionals have also documented cases of arrhythmias (irregular heart rhythms) and sudden cardiac death following the consumption of these products. Some of these incidents involved young adults who had no previously identified risk factors for heart disease.

A 2026 American Heart Association Scientific Statement on caffeine and cardiovascular disease indicates that most adults can generally consume up to 400 mg of caffeine daily without significant safety concerns (the equivalent of up to 5, 8-ounce cups of regular black caffeinated coffee).

Industry observers note that however, caffeine concentrations can differ dramatically between products. Certain energy drinks provide up to three times as much caffeine per fluid ounce as brewed coffee, while some pre-workout supplements contain more than 12 times the concentration found in coffee.

It has been revealed that another concern involves how these products are regulated. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) classifies energy drinks and stimulant supplements as foods or dietary supplements rather than medications. As a result, they are not subject to the same safety testing requirements that medications must meet before entering the market.

According to recent reports, "These products are marketed as everyday pick-me-ups and sold next to soda and bottled water, so most people assume they carry no real risk," said study author Sai Samayamanthula, a fourth-year medical student at the University of Virginia School of Medicine in Charlottesville, Virginia. "For many healthy people, if these products are consumed occasionally, the risk is probably small. However, individuals who consume energy drinks or other stimulant-containing supplements regularly can quickly exceed the recommended daily limit for caffeine, so it's key for people to know that there may be a risk of cardiovascular harm with these products.".

FDA Reports Reveal Striking Differences in Cardiac Events.

To investigate possible cardiovascular safety concerns, researchers examined a federal database containing reports of suspected adverse reactions to foods and dietary supplements. They compared products containing caffeine and other stimulants with products that did not contain these ingredients.

It has been revealed that the comparison group included commonly consumed products such as soft drinks, smoothies, vitamins, protein bars, and meal replacement shakes. Researchers examined reports involving people ages 13 and older submitted between 2017 and 2025.

Several differences stood out in the analysis:.

These differences describe how frequently certain medical problems appeared within the FDA reports. They do not mean that people consuming energy drinks face an 11 times greater actual risk of cardiac arrest or a 4.5 times greater risk of having a heart attack.

"Our findings support the case for more systematic safety monitoring of caffeine- and stimulant-containing products. In addition, healthcare professionals should remember to ask their younger patients who have palpitations, chest pain, or fainting spells if they recently or regularly consume these products," Samayamanthula remarked.

Why Young Adults May Be Particularly Vulnerable.

One of the most notable findings was the large proportion of cardiovascular reports involving younger adults. Researchers have not yet determined why the connection between stimulant products and reported heart problems appeared so frequently in this age group.

Sources indicate that several explanations are possible. Younger consumers may use energy drinks and stimulant supplements more often, increasing the likelihood that these products appear in reports of medical emergencies.

How the products are consumed could also influence the pattern. Potential contributing factors include the circumstances surrounding their use (for example, consuming them before intense exercise or mixing them with alcohol or drugs). Some individuals may also have previously undiagnosed heart conditions that could make them more susceptible to cardiovascular complications.

These possibilities remain uncertain, and additional research will be needed to determine which factors, if any, help explain the unusually high reporting frequency among younger adults.

Do Energy Drinks Actually Cause Heart Attacks?

Although the results raise crucial questions about products containing concentrated caffeine and other stimulants, experts caution against interpreting the findings as proof of a direct cause.

Recent findings suggest that "This study raises concerns that products with very high amounts of caffeine may be harmful to the cardiovascular system," said Gregory M. Marcus, M.D., M.A.S., FAHA, chair of the 2026 American Heart Association scientific statement on caffeine and cardiovascular disease. "Although there are biological reasons why that connection could be possible, the study does not prove that caffeine products cause these events, because other factors may have influenced the results found in this analysis. More research is needed to understand whether these stimulant products are truly responsible for the reported heart-related events.".

Marcus did not participate in the research. He is a professor of medicine at the University of California, San Francisco School of Medicine and serves as associate chief of the Cardiology for Research program at the University of California, San Francisco Health.

Sources indicate that because the analysis relied on reports submitted voluntarily to the FDA, it cannot establish whether the products themselves were responsible for the cardiovascular events. Other health conditions, behaviors, or circumstances may have played a role.

How Researchers Analyzed the FDA Safety Reports.

The research team reviewed 28,345 reports of possible adverse events submitted to an FDA safety database from 2017 through 2025.

Of these, 854 reports involved energy drinks or dietary supplements containing caffeine or other stimulants. The remaining 27,491 reports concerned products without caffeine or stimulant ingredients and served as the comparison group.

Researchers classified products according to the ingredients they contained. The stimulant category included caffeine, methylxanthines (theobromine, guarana, yerba mate, green tea/coffee extracts) and sympathomimetics (synephrine, yohimbine, ephedra, DMAA, higenamine).

Rather than evaluating individual brands, the researchers grouped products by their ingredients. Consequently, the findings apply to broad categories of caffeinated and stimulant products and do not identify any particular brand as more dangerous than another.

The researchers also highlighted important limitations in the available data. Reports were voluntarily submitted by members of the public, consumers, healthcare professionals, and manufacturers, meaning that the database does not provide a complete record of everyone who experienced a possible adverse reaction.

Just as importantly, the researchers could not determine how many people consumed these products without developing cardiovascular problems. They also could not establish how many people experienced heart problems but never submitted a report.

Without those figures, the analysis cannot calculate the actual likelihood of a heart attack, cardiac arrest, or another cardiovascular event among consumers of energy drinks and stimulant supplements.

Recent findings suggest that nevertheless, the findings reveal a potentially important safety signal. Researchers say more systematic monitoring and further studies are needed to determine whether these products contribute directly to serious heart problems, particularly among younger adults who frequently consume them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elle and Dakota Fanning have been in the spotlight for decades, but their upcoming project, “The Nightingale,” marks the first time they’ve played sisters onscreen—an experience that brought them “closer” together, both on set and at home.

While they’ve visited each other on set in the past and even separately played different versions of the same character in the 2001 film “I Am Sam,” Elle, 28, told Vanity Fair that actually working with each other is a totally different ball game.

In a recent development, “It certainly brought us closer, which was hard to imagine—to be closer,” she mentioned. “Our mom always left us little notes in suitcases, like, ‘Just savor this time together. This is precious.’”.

Dakota, 32, confirmed that they took their mother’s advice.

It has been revealed that “We did really savor it,” she said. “And the biggest takeaway for me is when we have each other and when we’re together, we can do anything. That’s really how I feel. There’s nothing that I couldn’t do with Elle there with me.”.

It has been revealed that that said, the job wasn’t easy. The Fannings traveled to Budapest to shoot on location, where they lived together.

Recent findings suggest that “It was a challenging shoot, not going to lie. It was physically tiring, certainly emotionally taxing,” mentioned Elle.

After a long day of using lots of “brain power” on set, the sisters had to find a way to “recharge” each evening.

For Dakota and Elle, that meant eating lots of Thai food and streaming “The Real Housewives,” true crime, and “Margo’s Got Money Troubles”—the TV series the younger sister stars in, which was released while they filmed “The Nightingale.”.

Dakota revealed that on a day off, she’d often find herself cleaning up after Elle, which was poetic as her character, Vianne, also tidies her sister Isabelle’s mess.

Industry observers note that “Her bed in the mornings is like a tornado has run through it,” she remarked. “She’s just one of those sleepers. It’s all twisted into a crazy thing. I was like, ‘That’s no fun to get into a bed that’s all crumpled and rumpled. Let me make it nice.’”.

The older sister said that “it became a routine,” and she “always made her bed like that” when possible.

Elle said, “It’s art imitating life, because there’s even a scene where Vianne is making Isabelle’s bed, too.”.

Dakota and Elle were born in Conyers, GA. As young girls, they traveled between the Atlanta suburb and Los Angeles to work before relocating to the West Coast full time.

“When we were younger, we wanted to make sure that people saw us differently, and we wanted to give each other space to carve our own path,” Elle told Vanity Fair in 2025. “But as adults, it’s been very fulfilling to merge.”.

One of the most major ways the sisters have merged their lives in adulthood was in 2017, when they purchased a gorgeous $2.3 million property together.

According to Architectural Digest, they lived in a Cape Cod-style home in the Valley Village area of San Fernando Valley.

The 4,550-square-foot residence was perched at the end of a private, gated driveway and had a very classic aesthetic with white rose bushes planted along the front walkway.

The interiors were defined by delicate details, such as baby blue brocade-patterned walls, intricate chandeliers, and coffered ceilings.

The sisters sold the six-bedroom, six-bathroom estate for just under $2.7 million in May 2020.

It’s clear that Dakota was a fan of the dwelling’s traditional style, as she bought a very similar-looking home in Toluca Lake for $2.95 million in 2019, just before offloading the property she shared with Elle.

In a recent development, according to Architectural Digest, Dakota’s newer home spans 4,428 square feet and boasts five bedrooms and six bathrooms. It’s flooded with natural light and, like the first home, has crystal chandeliers, a pool in the backyard, and a double-height entry hall.

  • Sources indicate that coming five years after Intuit agreed to acquire Mailchimp for $12 billion, the sale price is less than a third of what the company paid.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 17:17 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

It has been revealed that financial software firm Intuit Inc. today revealed that it has agreed to sell its Mailchimp email marketing business to Italian technology holding company Bending Spoons S.p.A. for about $3.68 billion.

Sources indicate that coming five years after Intuit agreed to acquire Mailchimp for $12 billion, the sale price is less than a third of what the company paid. The 2021 purchase was the largest in Intuit’s history at the time.

It has been revealed that although Bending Spoons describes the transaction as all-cash, Intuit will reinvest $368 million of its proceeds in newly issued Bending Spoons shares. That leaves Intuit with $3.31 billion in cash from the sale, according to the companies. Included in the deal is The Rocket Science Group LLC, the legal entity behind Mailchimp. Closing is expected in early 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.

In a recent development, selling Mailchimp is stated to sharpen Intuit’s focus on the artificial intelligence-native tools it has built to help businesses win new customers, manage their pipeline and grow. Once the deal closes, Intuit intends to use the cash proceeds to buy back its own shares before the end of fiscal 2027.

Jack Tam, a senior vice president at Intuit, said the tech giant is confident Bending Spoons “will lead Mailchimp to continued success in this next chapter.”.

According to recent reports, growth at Mailchimp has stalled in recent quarters. Revenue from the business fell 1% to $313 million in the quarter ended Oct. 31. Intuit’s full-year guidance has Mailchimp revenue coming in flat to down 1%. In November 2024, Chief Financial Officer Sandeep Aujla told analysts that Intuit was seeing higher churn from smaller Mailchimp customers.

“Mailchimp is a powerful brand, built over two decades of reshaping the email marketing category and redefining how companies grow their audiences,” mentioned Luca Ferrari, co-founder and chief executive of Bending Spoons. “We’re honored to welcome it to Bending Spoons and excited about what we can accomplish together.”.

Ferrari added that Bending Spoons looks to invest substantially in Mailchimp after closing. According to Bending Spoons, the transformation of a business it acquires is typically deep, entailing reorganized teams, overhauled technology and redesigned user interfaces.

Recent findings suggest that founded in 2013, Bending Spoons has built a portfolio of digital businesses that includes AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Evernote, Tractive, Vimeo and WeTransfer. Since listing on the Nasdaq in July, the tech giant has also completed acquisitions of Airtable Inc. for $1.285 billion and whiteboard platform Miro for $1.355 billion.

Intuit announced the sale alongside its fiscal 2027 first-quarter results. For the quarter, it reported adjusted earnings per share of $2.91, up 56% from $1.87 in the same quarter of the previous year, on revenue of $4.35 billion, up 12% year-over-year. Analysts were expecting adjusted earnings of $2.70 per share on revenue of $4.31 billion.

For its fiscal second quarter, Intuit expects adjusted earnings per share of $3.17 to $3.22 on revenue of $4.93 billion to $4.95 billion. Intuit lowered its full-year revenue guidance to between $23.08 billion and $23.37 billion.

Behind the cut is Credit Karma, the company’s personal finance and credit score service, which is now forecast to grow 3% to 7% this fiscal year, down from 11% to 13% previously. Intuit reiterated its full-year adjusted earnings guidance of $22.88 to $23.12 per share. None of the guidance includes the effect of the Mailchimp sale.

Intuit shares fell more than 10% in after-hours trading.

Payer mix, non-labor expenses dragged hospital margins in September" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Hospitals’ operations took another dip in September amid a slew of ongoing headwinds including weakened payer mix and rising costs, healthcare advisory firm Kaufman Hall reported alongside warnings of a “historically large portion” of the nation’s hospitals running on negative or near-zero operating margins.

The firm’s latest monthly benchmark report, released Tuesday, revealed a calendar year-to-date operating margin index of 1.4% and a single-month operating margin index of 2.4% in September, the latter of which was a decline from August’s 3.0% operating margin (all including health system allocations for shared services costs).

The performance decline wasn’t for want of patients. Daily discharges and adjusted discharges both rose 3% from August to September, and are generally above the numbers from last year. Operating room minutes per calendar day also rose 6% from August—an encouraging sign for hospitals whose surgical slowdowns had hamstrung acuity—but remain 1% below September of last year.

Sources indicate that the increased foot traffic also grew revenues, with daily net operating revenue rising 4% from August and 6% year over year while gross operating revenue rose 4% month to month and 8% year over year. Much of the increase came on the outpatient side, where daily revenue increased 5% from August and 10% compared to September 2025. Net patient service revenue per adjusted discharge was more mixed, rising 2% from August but remaining 1% below September 2025.

However, hospitals’ margins are being challenged by persistent bad debt and charity care burdens, Kaufman Hall’s data show. Daily bad debt and charity care may have remained flat from August, but is 17% higher than September 2025 and 16% higher when comparing both years’ first nine months. As a percentage of gross operating revenue, they’re 6% higher than Sept. 2025 and 8% higher year to date.

On the spending side, daily total expense rose 3% from August and is 5% higher than September 2025, primarily reflecting the heightened volumes even as hospitals held their average length of stay flat month over month or 1% shorter year over year. The expenses were more pronounced on the non-labor side, where increases on a per adjusted discharge basis were higher than labor’s per adjusted discharge decline.

Recent findings suggest that "Hospitals continue to operate in an environment marked by significant financial variability," Erik Swanson, managing director and Data and Analytics group leader at Kaufman Hall, said in a release. “Many organizations continue to face mounting pressure from uncompensated care and rising expenses, underscoring the importance of proactive operational and financial strategies that build long-term resilience.".

Another amplifying market trend is the “bifurcation of hospital performance” often highlighted by the firm and others that monitor multi-organization financial trends, such as credit rating agencies.

Recent findings suggest that "The margin gap between higher and lower-performing hospitals has widened to 19 percentage points, with a historically large portion of hospitals operating at negative or very thin margins,” the report reads. “Even slight revenue reductions threaten organizations, which face increasingly difficult decisions on future operations, care delivery, and expense control.”.

The firm encouraged hospitals to take “deliberate, proactive steps” to strengthen their financial situations, particularly as macro reimbursement trends stiffen and the site of care delivery shifts from the hospital to outpatient settings.

Kaufman Hall’s hospital reports pull data from more than 1,300 nationwide hospitals as collected by parent organization Strata Decision Technology.

Accompanying the monthly hospital benchmark was also Kaufman Hall’s quarterly numbers on more than 200,000 employed physicians and advanced practice providers, which painted a much rosier picture for health system and hospital employers.

It showed, for the first time in five years of data collection, that healthcare employers’ investment/subsidy per provider and per physician has declined year over year (by 1%), and “across every cohort, including primary care, medical specialty, surgical specialty and hospital-based specialty.”.

Kaufman Hall attributed the rare turnaround to revenue growth and sustained productivity increases that together outpaced expenses.

According to recent reports, "Medical groups made meaningful performance improvements this quarter, achieving gains in revenue, productivity and thoughtful workforce management," Matthew Bates, managing director and Physician Enterprise Service Line leader at Kaufman Hall, said in a release. "The growing utilization of [advanced practice providers] and ongoing focus on operational and team effectiveness are helping organizations manage financial pressures while increasing access to care.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Four months after announcing their split, “The Real Housewives of Salt Lake City” cast member Angie Katsanevas and her estranged husband, Shawn Trujillo, are now living in separate homes.

“Recently, Shawn has bought a place that’s two minutes down the street. And I’m at home with Elektra,” Katsanevas revealed in a new People magazine interview.

According to recent reports, according to a Page Six report, Trujillo's new pad is a $1.1 million condo he purchased in September. The two-story dwelling spans 2,568 square feet and includes three bedrooms and 4.5 bathrooms.

The couple, who married in June 1999, have yet to legally divorce, but are "moving toward" that status.

Recent findings suggest that “We are separated. We haven’t put it on paper, but we are not reconciling as far as staying married,” the reality TV star, 53, explained. “I hate the massive D-word, but I’ll just have to say that, yeah, we are moving toward the big D.”.

The salon owner’s home—which viewers will recognize from the reality series—is a sprawling hillside estate that has been on and off the market for the past two years.

The four-bedroom, three-bathroom modern abode was first listed for $4.5 million in September 2024. The price was decreased to $4.38 million in March 2025, then to $3.85 million just two months later.

By December of last year, the listing was removed. It hit the market again in January 2026 for $3.85 million, where it sat for most of the year before being removed on Oct. 14.

Recent findings suggest that the couple purchased the 6,369-square-foot residence for an undisclosed sum in 2020. With soaring ceilings, white ash floors, and lots of sleek, marble surfaces, the modern abode has a distinct luxurious aesthetic.

The home has two primary suites, with one that includes a fireplace, sitting area, and double-vanity bathroom with a striking view of the surrounding Utah landscape. There are also dual walk-in closets.

The second is located on the main floor and also has two-walk in closets and a gorgeous bathroom.

Sources indicate that features in pairs seem to be a feature of the home in general, as there are also two kitchens. In addition to the chic white minimalist space at the center of the home, a concealed catering kitchen is equipped with Miele appliances, a separate refrigerator and freezer, and a space for staff to prepare food.

Industry observers note that it seems as if, despite the separation, daily life hasn’t changed too much in the home. Katsanevas noted that Trujillo stops by most days to pick up their 15-year-old daughter, Elektra, and take her to school.

It has been revealed that “He’ll come in and have coffee,” she explained. “He’ll bring her home from lessons, and we’ll have dinner together. We are still just spending time together. We’re best friends. We are peaceful, it’s positive. We have a lot to do together.”.

She noted that Trujillo remains close with her father and will celebrate the holidays with the family.

In a recent development, “My dad sends him all of his favorite dishes and continues to cook for him,” noted Katsanevas. “Shawn will spend Thanksgiving and Christmas with my family.”.

Although they are still connected in many ways, Katsanevas noted that after nearly three decades together, “space and doing things independently” have brought clarity.

In a recent development, “We are even going to different churches now,” she shared. “And that’s huge for me. We started out going to the same church.”.

Katsanevas also shut down rumors that she had initiated the split over their opposing political stances, a rumor that started after she cited their “different views” in a confessional interview during a recent episode of “The Real Housewives of Salt Lake City.”.

According to recent reports, “I’m not throwing a 30-year marriage away because of rumors or political views,” she mentioned. “There are so many things that Shawn and I have grown apart and have different views on, a lot of things at this stage of life. And it’s not one thing. It’s just, we’re very different people.”.

They’re still business partners, however, and are set to open a newly introduced hair salon together in Miami.

“We are continuing to grow our brand together, even though we are separated,” she said.

Katsanevas and Trujillo right now operate nine locations of their business, Lunatic Fringe Salon, across Utah, Ohio, and Idaho.

While she’s focused on remaining positive, Katsanevas remarked it took some time to work through the complicated feelings that accompanied the change.

Recent findings suggest that “It does take a minute to mourn the loss of the way your life once was and what it looked like,” she said. “I’ve processed, I’ve cried, I’ve accepted. I’ve had to swim away from the muddy waters to get to the clear water and say, ‘OK, I’m coming out of this and I’m going to be OK.’”.

#110790. Industry News: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
